name: nodebench-mcp-admin

tools.name: investigate
tools.description: Investigate a company, person, or topic and return a concise sourced artifact. This is the default v3 entry point: one ask in, one report-shaped output out.

subject.description: Company, person, or topic to investigate.

focus.description: Optional angle such as pricing, product, or market position.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Compare 2-4 entities using the same report-shaped output. The tool backfills quick diligence packets first so the comparison result is usable immediately.

tools.name: track
tools.description: Add, check, remove, or list tracked entities with one workflow tool. The default path optimizes for watched entities that can feed future nudges and brief artifacts.

note.description: Optional note saved alongside the tracking change.

tools.name: summarize
tools.description: Turn raw context into a compact brief with key points and optional persistence. This is the fast human-readable artifact when you do not need a full diligence packet.

save.description: Persist the summary into session memory. Defaults to true.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search across live web results and stored NodeBench knowledge in one call. Use this instead of deciding between external search and internal memory first.

tools.name: report
tools.description: Produce a human-readable artifact for either a research topic or a decision. If recommendation inputs are provided, this emits a memo. Otherwise it emits a diligence-style report.

topic.description: Topic or entity to report on.

tools.name: ask_context
tools.description: Ask against saved NodeBench context first. This searches session memory and the accumulated knowledge base so repeated setup and rediscovery costs stop compounding.

question.description: Question to ask against saved context.

tools.name: get_system_pulse
tools.description: Get a real-time health snapshot of the NodeBench MCP system. Returns database status, dashboard availability, embedding cache freshness, recent error rates, and overall health score (0-100). Think of it like a vital signs monitor — one glance tells you if the system is healthy.

include_dashboards.description: Check dashboard HTTP endpoints (adds ~1.5s latency). Default: true.

tools.name: get_drift_report
tools.description: Detect configuration and state drift in the NodeBench system. Checks for orphaned verification cycles, stale eval runs, database bloat, error rate spikes, embedding cache staleness, and notes accumulation. Each issue is classified as ok/warning/critical with healable flag. Think of it like a home inspection — it finds the leaky faucets before they become floods.

include_history.description: Include last 10 watchdog log entries for trend analysis. Default: false.

tools.name: run_self_heal
tools.description: Autonomous self-healing for detected drift issues. Fixes orphaned verification cycles (marks as abandoned), stale eval runs (marks as failed), and database bloat (prunes old logs, runs WAL checkpoint). Only fixes issues that are safe to auto-repair. Think of it like a house robot that cleans up messes — it only touches what it knows how to handle safely.

targets.description: Specific drift IDs to heal (e.g. ['orphaned_cycles', 'stale_evals', 'db_size']). Empty = heal all.

dry_run.description: If true, report what would be healed without actually doing it. Default: false.

tools.name: get_uptime_stats
tools.description: Get session uptime, tool call rates, error trends, and top tools over multiple time windows (5min, 1hr, 24hr, 7d). Includes error direction trend (increasing/decreasing/stable). Think of it like a car dashboard — speed, fuel level, and engine warning lights at a glance.

tools.name: set_watchdog_config
tools.description: Configure the background watchdog that continuously monitors system health. Set check interval, enable/disable, and adjust drift thresholds. Changes take effect immediately. Think of it like setting alarm sensitivity — too sensitive and you get noise, too loose and you miss real issues.

interval_minutes.description: Check interval in minutes (min: 1, max: 60). Default: 5.

db_size_mb.description: DB size warning threshold in MB (default: 500)

stale_cache_hours.description: Embedding cache staleness threshold in hours (default: 168)

tools.name: get_watchdog_log
tools.description: Get recent watchdog check results. Shows health score trend, detected issues, and auto-healed actions over time. Useful for understanding system behavior patterns. Think of it like a security camera playback — see what happened while you weren't looking.

limit.description: Number of recent entries to return (default: 20, max: 100)

only_issues.description: Filter to only show entries with warnings or criticals. Default: false.

tools.name: get_sentinel_report
tools.description: Get the latest sentinel self-test report with all 9 probe results (build, e2e, design, dogfood, voice, a11y, visual, performance, contract), root-cause diagnoses, and fix suggestions. The sentinel system is the 3-layer autonomous quality pipeline that tests the entire app surface.

probe_filter.description: Comma-separated probes to include (e.g. 'build,e2e,voice'). Default: all.

tools.name: get_observability_summary
tools.description: Unified observability summary combining MCP system pulse, sentinel probes, watchdog status, and maintenance recommendations. Best single tool for a quick health check before starting work.

tools.name: log_tool_call
tools.description: Log an MCP tool call for profiling. Called automatically by the NodeBench gateway to track tool usage patterns, cost, and latency. Returns whether the call was redundant.

toolName.description: Name of the MCP tool called

tools.name: get_session_profile
tools.description: Get the efficiency profile for the current session. Shows total calls, cost, latency, redundancy, and optimization suggestions.

tools.name: get_usage_insights
tools.description: Get aggregate usage insights across all sessions. Shows top tools, repeated queries, cost breakdown, and optimization opportunities. This is the founder operating intelligence layer.

daysBack.description: How many days of data to analyze (default: 7)

tools.name: suggest_optimizations
tools.description: Analyze the current session and suggest specific optimizations: cheaper models, cached results, workflow shortcuts, and reusable patterns.

tools.name: sync_daily_brief
tools.description: Sync daily brief + narrative data from Convex to local SQLite. Requires CONVEX_SITE_URL and MCP_SECRET environment variables. Returns sync summary with row counts and timing.

force.description: Force re-sync even if data already exists (default: false)

tools.name: get_daily_brief_summary
tools.description: Get the latest daily brief summary from local SQLite. Returns dashboard metrics, features, and source summary. No network needed — reads cached data.

tools.name: get_narrative_status
tools.description: Get narrative thread status from local SQLite. Returns threads grouped by phase (emerging, escalating, climax, resolution, dormant) with event counts. No network needed.

tools.name: get_ops_dashboard
tools.description: Get operational dashboard status from local SQLite. Returns last sync info, tool call frequency, active verification cycles, and data counts. No network needed.

tools.name: open_local_dashboard
tools.description: Start the local Daily Brief dashboard server if needed, and return the URL. The dashboard shows Brief metrics, Narrative thread lanes, and Ops status — all from local SQLite.

tools.name: open_operating_dashboard
tools.description: Start the Operating Dashboard — shows trajectory scores, event ledger, important changes, path replay, time rollups, packet readiness, and recent actions. The ambient intelligence surface for your business. All from local SQLite.

tools.name: start_autonomy_benchmark
tools.description: Start an autonomous capability benchmark. Defines a complex build challenge and tracks agent progress through milestones. Inspired by Anthropic's C-compiler test. Available challenges: c_compiler, rest_api, fullstack_app, cli_tool, data_pipeline. Call with challenge="list" to see all options.

challenge.description: Which challenge to run. Use "list" to see all available challenges.

projectPath.description: Absolute path where the project will be built (optional, for tracking)

notes.description: Any notes about the setup (model used, configuration, etc.)

tools.name: log_benchmark_milestone
tools.description: Record completion of a benchmark milestone. Tracks which milestones the agent achieved, time taken, tools used, and whether verification passed.

benchmarkId.description: The benchmark run ID from start_autonomy_benchmark

milestoneId.description: The milestone ID to mark as complete (e.g. 'lexer', 'auth', 'tests')

verificationPassed.description: Whether the milestone passed verification (tests, oracle comparison, etc.)

toolsUsed.description: List of NodeBench MCP tools used for this milestone

notes.description: Any notes about the implementation, challenges faced, or patterns discovered

durationMinutes.description: How long this milestone took (optional, for manual tracking)

tools.name: complete_autonomy_benchmark
tools.description: Finalize an autonomy benchmark run. Computes final score, duration, tool usage stats, and comparison against reference (e.g. Anthropic's C-compiler results). Call when the agent is done or stuck.

benchmarkId.description: The benchmark run ID to finalize

totalContextTokens.description: Estimated total context tokens consumed during the benchmark

notes.description: Final notes about the run (what worked, what didn't, key insights)

tools.name: run_benchmark_batch
tools.description: Run a longitudinal benchmark batch. N=1 is a smoke test (1 founder, 1 session). N=5 tests role generalization (5 users, different lenses). N=10 tests session stability (5 users × 2 sessions). N=100 tests compounding over time (10 users × 10 sessions). Returns a full batch report with RCA, PRR, and pass/fail gates.

layer.description: Benchmark layer: N1 (smoke), N5 (role variance), N10 (session stability), N100 (longitudinal)

tools.name: get_benchmark_history
tools.description: View historical benchmark batch results. Shows RCA and PRR trends over time. Filter by layer (N1/N5/N10/N100) to see specific benchmark levels.

tools.name: get_benchmark_report
tools.description: Get the full detailed report for a specific benchmark batch by batchId.

batchId.description: Batch ID from run_benchmark_batch or get_benchmark_history

tools.name: start_dogfood_session
tools.description: Start a new dogfood session for one of the 3 canonical loops (weekly_reset, pre_delegation, company_search). Returns sessionId for subsequent recording.

loopType.description: Which canonical dogfood loop is being tested

packetVersionUsed.description: Version/ID of the packet template being tested (optional)

tools.name: end_dogfood_session
tools.description: End a dogfood session with summary metrics: time-to-first-useful-output, delegation success, packet export status, and notes.

timeToFirstUsefulOutput.description: Milliseconds until first useful output was produced

tools.name: record_manual_correction
tools.description: Track a human correction to agent output. Every correction is evidence of a system gap — the system should have gotten this right.

afterValue.description: What the human corrected it to

tools.name: record_repeated_question
tools.description: Track a question the user asked that NodeBench should have already known. This is the core failure signal — repeat cognition means the system isn't compounding.

priorSessionId.description: Session where this was previously asked (optional)

tools.name: rate_packet_usefulness
tools.description: Rate a packet's real-world utility: was it exported, delegated, reused, or abandoned? How many human edits were needed?

packetType.description: Type of packet (weekly_reset, pre_delegation, company_search, etc.)

delegated.description: Was the packet delegated to someone?

reused.description: Was the packet reused in another context?

humanEditsCount.description: Number of human edits required before the packet was usable

tools.name: judge_session
tools.description: Score a dogfood session on 6 dimensions (1-5 each): truth, compression, anticipation, output, delegation, trust. Returns overall score and records failure classes.

truthQuality.description: 1-5: Were facts correct? Did it hallucinate?

compressionQuality.description: 1-5: Was context compressed without losing signal?

anticipationQuality.description: 1-5: Did it anticipate what you needed next?

delegationQuality.description: 1-5: Could you hand the output to someone without restatement?

trustQuality.description: 1-5: Did you trust the output enough to act on it?

tools.name: classify_failure
tools.description: Classify a failure by canonical system layer taxonomy. Tracks symptom, root cause, and system layer for structured triage.

judgeRunId.description: Judge run that identified this failure

tools.name: record_fix_attempt
tools.description: Record a fix attempt with replay proof and regression protection description. Links to a failure case.

replayProof.description: JSON proof: prior vs new scores

tools.name: get_dogfood_sessions
tools.description: List recent dogfood sessions with their judge scores. Filter by loop type.

tools.name: get_failure_triage
tools.description: Get open failure cases grouped by system layer with frequency counts. The triage board for fixing system gaps.

tools.name: get_regression_gate
tools.description: Check if the 3 canonical loops pass. Returns per-loop scores, overall pass/fail, and regression detection.

tools.name: get_repeat_cognition_metrics
tools.description: The key compound metric. Measures repeat question rate, manual reconstruction count, packet abandonment rate, delegation-without-restatement rate, and average time-to-useful-output.

tools.name: record_dogfood_telemetry
tools.description: Record a full telemetry row for a dogfood run. Captures surface, scenario, user role, prompt, tool usage, token estimates, latency, cost, and quality scores.

userRole.description: Role of the user running the scenario (default: founder)

primaryPrompt.description: The primary prompt/question that initiated this run

attachedInputs.description: Array of attached input descriptors (files, URLs, etc.)

inferredLens.description: The lens/perspective inferred for this run

stateBeforeHash.description: Hash of state before the run

stateAfterHash.description: Hash of state after the run

toolsInvoked.description: Array of tool names invoked during the run

repeatedQuestionPrevented.description: Whether a repeated question was prevented (default: unknown)

tools.name: detect_repeated_questions
tools.description: Analyze causal_events to find patterns where the user/agent asks the same strategic question repeatedly. Uses Jaccard similarity on summary text to cluster repeated queries.

lookbackDays.description: How many days to look back (default 30)

similarityThreshold.description: Jaccard similarity threshold to consider two questions repeated (0-1, default 0.6)

tools.name: get_dogfood_telemetry
tools.description: Query dogfood telemetry rows with optional filters. Returns matching rows plus computed averages (tool calls, latency, cost, judge score).

tools.name: judge_tool_output
tools.description: Run the 7-criterion LLM judge on a tool's output. Returns pass/fail per criterion with reasoning, overall verdict, and fix suggestions. Use after any dogfood tool call to validate quality. Criteria: (1) removed repeated cognition, (2) usable packet, (3) right contradiction, (4) noise suppressed, (5) downstream artifact, (6) causal memory updated, (7) trustworthy and reusable. Requires 5/7 to pass.

prompt.description: The original user prompt that was sent to the tool

toolName.description: Name of the tool that was called

result.description: The raw result object from the tool call

tools.name: run_judge_loop
tools.description: Execute a full judge-fix-verify loop: calls a tool, judges the output, and if it fails, returns the fix suggestions and failing criteria so you can fix and re-run. Use this for automated dogfood validation. Pass the tool name and args, and the loop will execute the tool, judge the result, and return the verdict with fix instructions.

toolArgs.description: Arguments to pass to the tool

tools.name: get_judge_history
tools.description: Get the history of LLM judge runs, optionally filtered by scenario. Shows pass/fail trends, common failures, and improvement over time.

tools.name: run_dogfood_batch_with_judge
tools.description: Execute the priority 3 dogfood scenarios with automatic LLM judge validation. Runs: (1) founder weekly reset, (2) Anthropic banker search, (3) context bundle injection. Each result is judged on 7 criteria. Returns a consolidated scorecard.

daysBack.description: Days to look back for context (default 7)

tools.name: start_execution_run
tools.description: Start a live Convex-backed execution trace run for a workflow. Creates a task session and trace together so later steps, decisions, evidence, verifications, and approvals all land on the same durable run.

title.description: Human-readable run title shown in NodeBench UI.

workflowName.description: Workflow label for the trace, e.g. 'Spreadsheet enrichment'. Defaults to title.

description.description: Short run purpose or operator instruction.

visibility.description: Whether the run is publicly visible in shared UI surfaces (default: private).

goalId.description: Optional Oracle/mission goal ID for cross-check tracking.

visionSnapshot.description: Optional immutable vision snapshot to anchor the run.

sourceRefs.description: Optional source references attached at run start.

metadata.description: Opaque metadata stored on both the session and trace.

tools.name: complete_execution_run
tools.description: Finish a live execution run by updating session status, trace status, and optional usage metrics. Use this after the workflow either completes or fails.

toolsUsed.description: Optional list of tools used during the run.

agentsInvolved.description: Optional list of agents involved in the run.

tools.name: record_execution_step
tools.description: Record a structured execution step receipt on a live execution trace. Use this for meaningful actions like file inspection, research queries, edits, exports, or issue fixes.

tools.name: record_execution_decision
tools.description: Record a structured decision on a live execution trace without storing raw hidden reasoning. Use for rankings, selections, rejections, or escalation logic grounded in evidence.

decisionType.description: Decision type, e.g. ranking, selection, rejection, escalation.

tools.name: record_execution_verification
tools.description: Record a verification result on a live execution trace. Use for render checks, formula checks, diff checks, artifact integrity checks, and issue-fix confirmations.

createGuardrailSpan.description: Whether to also create a guardrail span (default true).

tools.name: attach_execution_evidence
tools.description: Attach evidence to a live execution trace. Use for URLs, uploaded files, screenshots, render outputs, and truth-boundary notes that support or qualify the workflow output.

summary.description: What this evidence supports or qualifies.

tools.name: request_execution_approval
tools.description: Request a human approval gate for a risky execution-trace action. Approval state is written onto the live run so the UI and ledger can show the pending handoff.

toolArgs.description: Arguments or change payload for the risky action.

justification.description: Why approval is needed and what will happen if approved.

tools.name: overstory_fleet_status
tools.description: Read the Overstory multi-agent fleet status — active agents, capabilities, health, worktree state. Returns agent manifest configuration and live agent states from .overstory/overstory.db. Use this to monitor QA agent progress during a dogfood session.

include_config.description: Include agent manifest configuration (capabilities, models, constraints). Default true.

tools.name: overstory_qa_summary
tools.description: Aggregate QA gate results across all routes — per-route stability grades, issue counts by severity (p0-p3), gate pass/fail status, and freshness check. Combines data from visual_qa_runs (SSIM) and Overstory mail (Gemini QA triage).

hours.description: Only include data from the last N hours. Default 4.

tools.name: overstory_mail_log
tools.description: Read recent Overstory QA mail messages — capture-complete, stability results, triage reports, fix assignments, worker-done notices, and escalations. Useful for understanding the current state of a QA session.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Default 20.

type_filter.description: Filter by message type: result, dispatch, worker_done, escalation, error, status. Empty = all.

agent_filter.description: Filter by sender or recipient agent name. Empty = all.

tools.name: overstory_merge_queue
tools.description: Read the Overstory merge queue — pending merges, completed merges, conflict resolution status, and QA gate results per branch. Shows which builder branches are ready to merge and which are blocked.

tools.name: plan_decompose_mission
tools.description: Decompose a mission into subtasks with verifiability routing. Creates a run, task plan, and subtask assignments. Each subtask gets a verifiabilityTier (tier_1_machine | tier_2_expert), judgeMethod, retryBudget, and requiresHumanSniffCheck flag. Enforces: one owner per subtask, bounded input package, explicit output contract.

title.description: Mission title — what is the top-level goal?

description.description: Full mission description with context and constraints

ownerAgent.description: Assigned agent (one owner, no shared editing)

judgeMethod.description: How to verify this subtask's output

retryBudget.description: Max retry attempts before escalation (default: 3, max: 5)

requiresSniffCheck.description: Whether human sniff-check is required before merge

inputPackage.description: Bounded input — what data/context this subtask receives

outputContract.description: Explicit output contract — what this subtask must produce

dependsOn.description: Indices (0-based) of subtasks this depends on

rationale.description: Why this decomposition was chosen (for traceability)

tools.name: judge_verify_subtask
tools.description: Judge verifies a subtask's output against its output contract. Records verdict (pass/fail), reasoning, evidence references, and recommended action (pass/retry/replan/escalate/stop). Creates artifacts and evidence records for full traceability.

verdict.description: Did the subtask meet its output contract?

reasoning.description: Judge's reasoning for the verdict (full traceability, no hidden CoT)

score.description: Optional numeric score (0-1). No hardcoded floors — 0 means 0.

action.description: Recommended next action based on verdict

tools.name: judge_request_retry
tools.description: Request a retry, re-plan, escalation, or stop for a failed subtask. Enforces retry budget — if exhausted, auto-escalates. Actions: pass | retry | replan | escalate | stop. If action is 'stop', marks subtask as unverifiable.

reviewId.description: Judge review ID that triggered this

newInstructions.description: Updated instructions for retry/replan (what to do differently)

tools.name: merge_compose_output
tools.description: Judge-gated merge of subtask artifacts into a composed output. Only merges subtasks that have passed verification. Enforces: no shared free-for-all editing — merge boundary is explicit. Optionally requires judge review of the merged output.

subtaskIds.description: Subtask IDs to merge (must all be passed)

mergedOutput.description: The composed output from merging subtask artifacts

requiresJudgeReview.description: Whether the merged output needs judge review before finalization

tools.name: sniff_record_human_review
tools.description: Record a human sniff-check for a subtask or merge output. Verdicts: pass | concern | block. Issue tags: unsupported_claim, weak_evidence, not_credible, too_risky, scope_drift, missing_source, contradictory, stale_data. If verdict is 'block', creates a force-retry path.

subtaskId.description: Subtask ID being reviewed (mutually exclusive with mergeId)

mergeId.description: Merge boundary ID being reviewed (mutually exclusive with subtaskId)

verdict.description: pass = approved, concern = flagged but proceed, block = force retry

tools.name: harness_get_mission_status
tools.description: Get full mission execution status: run info, subtask states, judge reviews, sniff-checks, merge boundaries, and traceability receipts. Read-only query for the Mission Graph / Live Execution Board.

includeEvidence.description: Include evidence records (default: false for performance)

tools.name: harness_list_runs
tools.description: List all mission runs with status summary. Supports filtering by status. For the Live Execution Board.

tools.name: compute_dimension_profile
tools.description: Recompute and persist the DeepTrace dimension profile for an entity. Use after new company evidence, relationship updates, or temporal signals land.

entityName.description: Optional display name when entity context is sparse

entityType.description: Optional entity type such as company or person

triggerEventKey.description: Optional event key or reason for recomputation

tools.name: get_dimension_profile
tools.description: Fetch the latest persisted DeepTrace dimension profile, including regime label, policy context, confidence, and the normalized dimension state.

tools.name: list_dimension_snapshots
tools.description: List historical DeepTrace dimension snapshots for an entity to inspect regime transitions over time.

limit.description: Maximum number of snapshots to return (default 12)

tools.name: list_dimension_evidence
tools.description: List the durable evidence rows behind a DeepTrace dimension profile. Useful for auditing why a score or availability status was assigned.

dimensionFamily.description: Optional family such as capital, people, or narrative

dimensionName.description: Optional metric name within the family

tools.name: list_dimension_interactions
tools.description: List stored interaction effects for an entity, such as capital plus investor quality reducing execution fragility or narrative outpacing evidence.

tools.name: export_dimension_bundle
tools.description: Export the full DeepTrace dimension bundle for an entity: latest profile, snapshots, evidence, and interaction effects in one response.

tools.name: run_research_cell
tools.description: Run a bounded re-analysis cell for a DeepTrace entity investigation. Queries existing DeepTrace state through parallel branches (evidence gap analysis, counter-hypothesis, dimension coverage, source diversification) to surface gaps and weaknesses. Does NOT acquire new external evidence — use due-diligence orchestrator for that. Triggers when confidence is low, coverage is sparse, or operator requests deeper analysis. Returns merged findings in standard DeepTrace format with receipts and dimension profile.

confidence.description: Current investigation confidence [0,1]. Cell auto-triggers below 0.65

dimensionCoverage.description: Current dimension coverage ratio [0,1]. Cell auto-triggers below 0.70

durableSourceCount.description: Number of durable evidence sources. Cell auto-triggers below 3

operatorRequested.description: Force-trigger the research cell regardless of thresholds

existingFacts.description: Known facts to avoid redundant research

tools.name: run_entity_intelligence_mission
tools.description: Run a full DeepTrace entity intelligence mission with optional bounded research cell. Unifies relationship mapping, ownership, supply chain, signals, and causal analysis. Pass researchCell=true for threshold-driven re-analysis when the investigation has gaps, or forceResearchCell=true to explicitly force the bounded cell.

researchCell.description: Enable threshold-driven autoresearch cell for low-confidence investigations

forceResearchCell.description: Force the bounded research cell even if thresholds are healthy

tools.name: run_quality_gate
tools.description: Evaluate content or code against a set of boolean rules. Returns pass/fail with specific failures listed. The agent evaluates each rule and passes boolean results — the tool persists and aggregates.

gateName.description: Name for this gate (e.g. 'engagement', 'code_review', 'deploy_readiness', or custom)

target.description: What is being checked (content text, file path, PR description)

tools.name: get_gate_preset
tools.description: Get the rules for a built-in quality gate preset. Returns rule names, descriptions, and evaluation instructions so you can check each one. Presets: engagement (content quality), code_review (implementation quality), deploy_readiness (pre-deploy checklist), ui_ux_qa (frontend UI/UX verification), agent_bug_verdict (evidence-first QA verdict discipline), agent_comparison (A/B agent eval), a11y (WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit), visual_regression (baseline visual diff checks).

tools.name: get_gate_history
tools.description: Get the history of quality gate runs for a given gate name. Shows pass/fail trend over time.

tools.name: run_closed_loop
tools.description: Track a compile-lint-test-debug closed loop iteration. Record the result of each step. Never present changes without a full green loop.

cycleId.description: Optional: link to a verification cycle

tools.name: start_eval_run
tools.description: Start a new eval run. Define the test batch upfront with test cases (input, intent, expected behavior), then record results as each case is executed. Rule: no change ships without an eval improvement.

intent.description: What the agent should accomplish (ground truth)

tools.name: record_eval_result
tools.description: Record the actual result for a specific eval case. Include what happened, the verdict (pass/fail/partial), and optionally telemetry data and judge notes.

telemetry.description: Tool calls, latency, errors — any execution trace data

judgeNotes.description: LLM judge analysis: goal alignment, tool efficiency, output quality, suggestions

tools.name: complete_eval_run
tools.description: Finalize an eval run and compute aggregate scores. Returns pass rate, average score, failure patterns, and improvement suggestions.

tools.name: compare_eval_runs
tools.description: Compare two eval runs to decide whether a change should ship. Returns side-by-side scores and a deploy/revert recommendation. Rule: no change ships without an eval improvement.

candidateRunId.description: The new eval run after changes

tools.name: list_eval_runs
tools.description: List recent eval runs with their aggregate scores. Use this to track quality over time and detect drift.

tools.name: diff_outputs
tools.description: Compare two text or JSON outputs and produce a structured diff with similarity score. Use for model comparison, oracle validation, before/after analysis, or regression detection. Returns added/removed/changed elements with a human-readable summary.

format.description: Comparison format: 'text' for line-by-line, 'json' for field-level, 'auto' to detect (default: 'auto')

tools.name: start_verification_cycle
tools.description: Start a new 6-phase verification cycle for a non-trivial implementation. Returns the cycle ID and Phase 1 instructions. Call this before declaring any integration, migration, or protocol-level change done.

title.description: What you are verifying (e.g. 'MCP protocol compliance', 'Auth migration')

description.description: Context about the change being verified

tools.name: log_phase_findings
tools.description: Record findings for the current phase of a verification cycle. Advances the cycle to the next phase if the current phase passes. If it fails, returns guidance to loop back.

tools.name: log_gap
tools.description: Record a gap found during Phase 2 (Gap Analysis). Gaps are categorized by severity: CRITICAL (protocol violations, security), HIGH (API incompatibilities), MEDIUM (outdated versions), LOW (edge cases).

tools.name: resolve_gap
tools.description: Mark a gap as resolved after implementing the fix. Returns remaining gap counts by severity.

resolution.description: What was done to fix it

tools.name: log_test_result
tools.description: Record a test result for Phase 4 (Testing & Validation). Tests are organized by layer: static, unit, integration, manual, live_e2e. All layers must pass before proceeding.

tools.name: get_verification_status
tools.description: Get the current status of a verification cycle including all phases, gaps, and test results. Use this to understand where you are in the process and what to do next.

tools.name: list_verification_cycles
tools.description: List all verification cycles, optionally filtered by status. Use this to find a cycle ID or review past verifications.

status.description: Filter by status (optional, returns all if omitted)

tools.name: abandon_cycle
tools.description: Abandon an active verification cycle that will not be completed. Use this to clean up orphaned or stale cycles.

cycleId.description: The verification cycle ID to abandon

reason.description: Why this cycle is being abandoned (optional)

tools.name: findTools
tools.description: Search available methodology tools by keyword or capability description. Returns matching tool names and descriptions. Use this to discover which tools are available for a task.

query.description: What you want to do (e.g. "verify implementation", "track quality", "record edge case")

tools.name: getMethodology
tools.description: Get step-by-step guidance for a development methodology. Topics: verification, eval, flywheel, mandatory_flywheel, reconnaissance, quality_gates, ui_ux_qa, flywheel_ui_dogfood, agentic_vision, closed_loop, learnings, project_ideation, tech_stack_2026, telemetry_setup, agents_md_maintenance, agent_bootstrap, autonomous_maintenance, parallel_agent_teams, self_reinforced_learning, academic_paper_writing, agent_evaluation, controlled_evaluation, scenario_testing, overview. Call with topic "overview" to see all available methodologies.

tools.name: check_mcp_setup
tools.description: Comprehensive diagnostic wizard for the entire NodeBench MCP. Checks all env vars, API keys, optional npm packages, and external services across every domain. Returns a full readiness report with per-domain status and step-by-step setup instructions for anything missing. Run this FIRST to see what capabilities are available and what needs configuration.

domains.description: Specific domains to check (default: all). Options: web, vision, github, llm, embedding, email, flicker_detection, figma_flow, ui_capture, local_file, gaia_solvers

test_connections.description: Test reachability of Python servers (flicker on :8006, figma on :8007) and email SMTP/IMAP. Default: false

generate_config.description: Generate a complete MCP config snippet with all needed env vars (default: true)

generate_setup.description: Generate complete setup files that an agent can write to disk to self-enable every capability: .env.nodebench (env template), setup-nodebench.sh (bash), setup-nodebench.ps1 (powershell), docker-compose.nodebench.yml (Python servers). Default: false

tools.name: discover_tools
tools.description: Multi-modal tool search engine with 14 scoring strategies: keyword, fuzzy (typo-tolerant), n-gram (partial words), prefix, semantic (synonym expansion), TF-IDF (rare tags score higher), regex, bigram (phrase matching), domain cluster boosting, dense (TF-IDF cosine), neural embedding tool RRF, domain RRF (Agent-as-a-Graph bipartite graph), upward traversal (tool→domain→siblings), and execution trace edges (co-occurrence mining). Returns ranked results with quick refs. Use mode='hybrid' (default) for best results, or 'regex'/'fuzzy'/'prefix'/'semantic'/'exact'/'dense'/'embedding' for targeted search.

query.description: Natural language description of what you want to do (e.g. "verify my implementation", "search past findings", "run tests", "write academic paper")

limit.description: Max results to return per page (default: 10)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination (default: 0). Use with limit to page through results. Response includes totalMatches and hasMore.

expand.description: Expand top-N results by including their relatedTools neighbors at 50% parent score (default: 0 = no expansion). Use expand=3 to discover adjacent tools.

includeChains.description: Also return matching workflow chains (default: true)

mode.description: Search mode. 'hybrid' (default) runs all strategies including neural embeddings when available. 'fuzzy' tolerates typos. 'regex' accepts patterns. 'prefix' matches tool name starts. 'semantic' expands synonyms. 'exact' requires exact match. 'dense' uses TF-IDF cosine similarity. 'embedding' uses neural embedding similarity only.

explain.description: Include matchReasons array showing which search strategies contributed to each result's score (default: false)

intent.description: High-level intent hint. Narrows the search to the most relevant toolsets BEFORE running hybrid search. Use this when you know the domain but not the exact tool. Reduces noise and improves accuracy.

compact.description: Return compact results with just name, category, and a one-line hint (saves ~60% tokens in the response). Default: false.

tools.name: get_tool_quick_ref
tools.description: Get the quick reference for a specific tool: what to do next, related tools, methodology, and tips. Call this after using any tool to understand the recommended next step in the workflow.

toolName.description: The name of the tool to get quick ref for

includeRelatedDetails.description: Also return quick refs for the recommended next tools (default: false)

tools.name: get_workflow_chain
tools.description: Get a recommended tool sequence for a common workflow. Returns step-by-step tool chain with actions for each step across feature dev, debugging, security, deployment, research, academic writing, CI/CD, multi-agent coordination, content production, and more. Call with chain="list" to see all.

chain.description: Which workflow chain to retrieve. Use "list" to see all available chains with descriptions.

tools.name: get_tool_graph
tools.description: Returns a JSON graph of tool relationships that grows with usage. Nodes represent tools, edges represent relationships (nextTool, relatedTool, cooccurrence). Use rootTool to focus on a subgraph, depth to control traversal, includeUsage to add execution counts. Default: starts from discover_tools at depth 2, up to 100 nodes.

rootTool.description: Tool name to start the graph traversal from (default: discover_tools). Set to empty string to get the full graph.

depth.description: How many hops to traverse from the root tool (default: 2, max: 5). Ignored when rootTool is empty.

includeUsage.description: Include usage counts and last-used timestamps from execution trace (default: true). Requires SQLite tool_call_log table.

tools.name: load_toolset
tools.description: Dynamically load a toolset into the current session. After loading, the tools become immediately available for use. Based on the "Search+Load" architecture from Dynamic ReAct (arxiv 2509.20386) — the winning pattern for scalable MCP tool selection. Use discover_tools first to find which toolset you need, then call this to activate it.

toolset.description: Toolset name to load. Available: learning, flywheel, autonomous_delivery, sync_bridge, shared_context, recon, ui_capture, vision, local_file, web, github, docs, bootstrap, self_eval, parallel, llm, security, platform, research_writing, flicker_detection, figma_flow, boilerplate, session_memory, workspace, gaia_solvers, toon, pattern, git_workflow, seo, voice_bridge, critter, email, rss, architect, ui_ux_dive, mcp_bridge, ui_ux_dive_v2, skill_update, visual_qa, design_governance, agent_traverse, engine_context, context_sandbox, research_optimizer, web_scraping, thompson_protocol, sweep, monte_carlo, temporal_intelligence, deep_sim, founder, entity_enrichment, scenario_compiler, packet_compiler, plan_synthesis, entity_temporal, entity_lookup, site_map, savings, delta, subconscious, claude_code_ingest, graphify

tools.name: unload_toolset
tools.description: Remove a dynamically loaded toolset from the current session to free up context. Cannot unload toolsets from the initial preset.

tools.name: list_available_toolsets
tools.description: List all available toolsets showing which are currently loaded and which can be dynamically added. Includes tool counts and descriptions for each toolset.

tools.name: call_loaded_tool
tools.description: Call a dynamically loaded tool by name. Use this after load_toolset when your client does not automatically refresh the tool list. Pass the tool name and its arguments. Example: call_loaded_tool({ tool: "analyze_screenshot", args: { imagePath: "screenshot.png" } }). This is a fallback — if the loaded tool appears in your tool list directly, call it directly instead.

tool.description: Name of the dynamically loaded tool to call.

args.description: Arguments to pass to the tool (same as its inputSchema).

tools.name: smart_select_tools
tools.description: LLM-powered tool selection: sends your task description + a compact tool catalog to a fast model (Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5-mini, or Claude Haiku 4.5) to pick the best 5-10 tools. Much more accurate than keyword search for ambiguous queries like "call an AI model" or "analyze my data". Requires GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Falls back to heuristic discover_tools if no API key is set.

task.description: Describe what you want to accomplish. Be specific. Example: 'I need to parse a PDF, extract tables, and email a summary'

provider.description: Which LLM provider to use. 'auto' (default) picks the first available API key.

tools.name: get_ab_test_report
tools.description: Generate an A/B test comparison report for static vs dynamic toolset loading. Shows session counts, tool counts, load events, error rates, and per-toolset load frequency. Use after running sessions in both modes to evaluate the impact of dynamic loading.

detailed.description: Include per-session breakdown (default: false, summary only)

instructions:
NodeBench MCP provides structured AI development methodology tools.
Use NodeBench tools when you need to:
- Verify implementations (verification cycles, gap tracking, 6-phase flywheel)
- Run evaluations and quality gates before shipping code
- Search prior knowledge and record learnings across sessions
- Assess risk before taking actions
- Coordinate parallel agents (task locks, roles, context budget)
- Research with structured recon (web search, GitHub, RSS feeds)
- Analyze files (CSV, PDF, XLSX, images, audio, ZIP)
- Run security audits (dependency scanning, code analysis, secrets detection)
- Write and polish academic papers
- Audit SEO, analyze Figma flows, detect Android flicker
- Call LLMs (GPT, Claude, Gemini) for analysis and extraction
Start with discover_tools("<your task>") to find the right tool.
